audit_method: Independent standard-library raw-byte hash and event/inventory/accounting fold; did not rerun native tests, regenerate proofs or call the original Python verifier.

definitions.completed_attempt: Honest completion, private target miss at candidate check, or successful private proof completion; private-check winner and private-complete are one attempt.
definitions.cpu_reconciliation: Unique per-attempt preparation/proof/verification CPU + native admission/notification event CPU + retained other process CPU = whole run process CPU.
definitions.honest_stale_completed_delivery: An honest packet completed and queued, then its parent differs from receiver selected_before when delivered. Private fork publications are excluded from this count.
definitions.modeled_time: Declared logical ticks; process wall/CPU are eager observer measurements. Queue propagation accounting is derived logical occupancy, not a physical transfer measurement.
definitions.receiver_selection_change: A receiver-admit event with selected_before != selected_after, split by packet producer.

limitations: Twelve bounded four-second receiver-following experiments with at most six honest starts and two private attempts; not an ongoing arbitrary public network.
Observer-advice runs are separately labeled prior winner-census controls and are not blind fixed-policy success estimates.
Every q>0 private search is censored before candidate completion; no quantum candidate or Grover output was fabricated.
Actual execution uses CPU native programs and exact packet rules; quantum service clocks remain stated model premises.
No calibrated physical quantum hardware, exhaustive native honest probability law, equal total real resource proof, global algorithm lower bound or long-term settlement proof.
The audit verifies consistency and retained bytes. It does not independently attest the original execution environment or repeat the cryptographic/W1 computations.
